summary: Full regression of the new Law/Crime/Imprisonment/Trial/Escape system plus dependent subsystems (NPC memory, companions, image storage, public Chronicle, scene-state). 17/17 pytest tests pass; frontend Rap Sheet modal, Admin Law tab, WANTED banner (same-nation propagation + cross-nation isolation), and Surrender button all verified live against the production-preview URL.

minor.issue: Returns ETag header (good) but Cache-Control is 'no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate', which neuters the browser cache benefit the refactor was aiming for. Recommend Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400, immutable for the deterministic image id route.
HEAD is not allowed (405). Add HEAD support to make ETag/If-None-Match conditional GETs from CDNs/browsers cheaper.

AI trial for capital/regicide deterministically returns sentence_type='execute' which immediately flips is_active=false on the character. There is no admin reactivate endpoint, so an executed test character is unrecoverable via API (had to flip is_active in Mongo). Recommend (a) an admin /api/admin/characters/{id}/revive endpoint, and (b) softening the AI prompt to allow imprison for capital tier in some cases, or skipping is_active flip for testing-flagged characters.

issues: Radix Dialog warning in console: 'Missing Description or aria-describedby for DialogContent' — add a DialogDescription for accessibility.

action_items: Soften AI trial verdict for capital crimes OR add an admin character-revive endpoint so executed characters can be restored (currently requires Mongo write).
Tighten Cache-Control on /api/image/{id} to actually permit browser caching (long max-age + immutable since IDs are content-stable).
Add HEAD method handler on /api/image/{id} so CDNs can do cheap freshness checks.
Add DialogDescription to RapSheet.js to silence the Radix a11y warning.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 4652 lines — overdue for modularisation (law endpoints, image endpoints, admin endpoints could each live in their own router file).
Trial AI verdict has no guard rail — a single bad LLM response can permanently 'execute' a player character without manual DB intervention. Consider a max-severity policy or admin-override path.
test_law_system.py currently relies on AI non-determinism (xfail on creative escape failure); for stability, consider providing a deterministic-stub mode behind an env flag for CI.

success_rate.frontend: 100% on visited flows (Rap Sheet modal, Admin Law tab, WANTED banner propagation + cross-nation isolation, Surrender button)

seed_data_creation: Did not create seed users. Did create temporary crimes / imprisonments / owned-npcs for the test character (a35a8ce2-71db-467c-8ad0-451fe9433a87 = 'Ausar Veltraus'); all cleaned up after the run via DELETE /api/admin/crimes/{id}, POST /api/admin/imprisonments/{id}/release, DELETE /api/owned-npcs/{id} and a final Mongo sweep that also reset is_active=true.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: pytest /app/backend/tests/test_law_system.py -v --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/law_system.xml. Test character is the first one returned by GET /api/characters under the admin account. The fixture auto-cleans crimes/imprisonments around the run. If the AI trial executes the character (sentence_type='execute'), it sets is_active=false — you'll need to revive via Mongo until an admin /revive endpoint ships. WANTED banner verified at /roleplay/ammeonon/wymroost and /roleplay/ammeonon/azure-castle (propagates) and NOT at /roleplay/dhor-khuldor/anchor-smithy (cross-nation isolation correct).
rca of the issue: No blocking bugs. The only real RCA worth recording: the surrender→trial flow for capital-tier crimes returns sentence_type='execute' deterministically, which made the imprisonment/escape pytest cases skip on the first run. Reproduction: commit a murder of a noble in /api/locations/ammeonon/wymroost/roleplay, then POST /api/characters/{id}/surrender — body.trial.sentence_type='execute', body.imprisonment=null. Mitigation in tests: clear capital/regicide crimes first and surrender on a freshly-recorded minor/major crime (shoplifting+assault). Long-term mitigation: AI prompt tuning or an admin revive endpoint.
